I've finished the title anatomy. The data backs the current launch title, "Hawaii Is Only the Summit. We Measured the Rest." (48 characters), and the niche report's two short backup titles score poorly enough that I'd replace them as backups.

**Data.** I ran 103 searches (73 from this morning plus 30 new) and pulled 1,424 channel pages. The table has 6,528 long-form titles from 1,227 channels, with views, age and channel size on 6,473 of them. "Views relative to channel size" means a video's views divided by that channel's typical views. The deciding test compares each channel's own videos with each other (285 channels), which removes channel size and quality. Simply ranking the top 10% across all channels mostly picks up tiny channels' one-off hits: their median channel has 28K subscribers against 103K for the median group.

**Findings, measured on the same channel:**
- **The promise matters more than the shape.**
  - Access ("can't visit / can't reach") got 1.56x the channel's usual views.
  - "Every X" got 1.81x.
  - Transformation (what if, without, drained) is the strongest signal across the whole sample, 1.7–2.0x. But all its words are clone vocabulary, so it has to come from the image and the first spoken line.
- **Short titles lose.** Titles of 40 characters or fewer got 0.81x; 41–50 characters scored 1.03x. Aim for 41–50. The craft channels' 44–47 median is a house style, not what drives views.
- **Several standing rules turn out to be style, not levers.** Questions, numbers, ALL-CAPS and the place name in the first 3 words made no difference. The place name in the first 3 words is actually a clone marker (31% of clone titles vs 13% of craft). Keep "Hawaii" in the title for matching with the big Hawaii videos, but its position doesn't matter.
- **Word choice:**
  - Brackets help (1.30x), most of all when they add a twist (1.56x).
  - Fear words lose (0.79x).
  - Every (1.82x), deepest (1.49x), isolated (1.41x) and lost (1.33x) win.
- **These formulas underperform their own channels:** "Why X", "How X", number lists and yes/no questions (0.71–0.79x). "X Is Hiding Something" is the worst at 0.60x.
- **Banning the clone words costs a little.** In non-clone channels those words still got 1.18x ("bottom" 3.4x). Banning them is a choice for distinctiveness and trust, not a free win.

**For ep02:**
- **Keep the launch title.** Today's probe of the exact title found no matches. One condition: "We Measured" is only honest if the film shows the measurement on the real survey data and says "about 56,000 feet, from its true base".
- **First swap if it stalls:** "Hawaii Is Only the Summit. You Can't See the Rest." (50 characters, no probe matches). It changes only the second sentence, from proof to an access gap.
- **Demote** "Hawaii, Measured From Its True Base" and "Hawaii Is Only the Summit" to the description and chapter titles; both are under 41 characters.
- **Reject** these:
  - "How Tall Is Hawaii, Really?", which the probe places among Hawaii travel videos and next to the 14M "Hawaii Is Much Bigger Than You Think" Short.
  - "...the Tip", which pulls in tipping-culture videos.
  - "Hawaii Is Much Taller Than You Think", which is a spent hook (that same 14M Short).
  - The "Underwater" titles, which read as flood news.
- **For the thumbnail step:** a postcard that says "HAWAII" repeats the title's first word, which goes against packaging rule P6.
- **Later episodes:** 9 of the 10 ep03–ep12 working titles are 40 characters or fewer, and ep04 uses "Never", which is on the avoid list.

The report has the formula library (20 formulas ranked, 3 real examples each), 12 banned patterns with evidence, and 16 candidate titles checked.

Limits: these are view measurements, since CTR isn't public. The topic filter misses some in-space titles with no geography word, such as the 4.4M "Why Can't You Visit Iwo Jima?". Drain-only and farm-only channels can't be tested channel-by-channel because they post nothing else.

**Shared files:** I replaced `work/raw/filtered.json` with a version that includes today's new searches (the old one is kept as `work/raw/filtered_v1.json`) and added 244 channels to `work/raw/channels.json`. Another agent is writing into `packaging/anat/`; I didn't touch it. The packaging folder is 86 MB in total.

I saved the thumbnail anatomy report and the 15-exemplar contact sheet. The packaging folder is 90 MB, under the 300 MB limit. The main finding is that colour does not predict a winning thumbnail in this space. Brightness, saturation and colourfulness do not separate the top performers from the rest, and the winners are slightly darker.

**Data.** I collected 247 thumbnails:
- the 106 already coded by the niche study;
- 95 new ones from this morning's packaging pull;
- 46 from fresh probes today, covering the missing context.md outliers, topic_hunt.json incumbents, and the Hawaii, volcano, seamount, Everest-vs-Mauna-Kea, islands and maps clusters.

232 have known views and channel size, and 203 are at least 7 days old and at least 4 minutes long. I computed the image measures with PIL and coded the visual features by eye from shuffled sheets with no titles or views shown. My codes agree 81-100% with the niche study's codes.

**Split.** A top performer has at least 100K views and at least 10x its channel's subscriber count: 63 videos against 140 for the rest. I checked the results three other ways: small channels only, views against the channel's own median, and craft channels only.

**Findings:**
- **Brightness and colour:** winners are a little darker, with median brightness 90 vs 104 on a 0-255 scale (p=0.016). Bright or saturated pixels cover 21% of the frame vs 27% (p=0.008). Partly this is topic, since deep-ocean videos are dark by nature. Only 13% of winners meet rule P5's "40% bright or saturated".
- **Text:** winners use a median of 4 words, or 3.5 once collage grids are removed. The tallest line is a median 10% of thumbnail height in both groups. Only 6 of 233 thumbnails with text reach P5's 20%. Among small channels, the rest actually use bigger text than the winners (12% vs 10%).
- **Graphic devices:** arrows, rings, red highlighted regions, before/after splits, depth labels and caption boxes are equally common in both groups. 84% of winners use at most one, and 54% use none. Among craft channels, caption boxes appear on 6% of winners vs 23% of the rest (p=0.008).
- **What goes with underperforming:** faces and scale comparisons.
  - The 7 Everest / tallest-mountain videos include no top performer. Their median is 0.77x their channel's usual views, against 9.6x for the whole set.
  - Against the 10 videos that fell below their own channel's median, faces appear in 5% of winners vs 30%, and scale comparisons in 5% vs 30%.
  - This backs keeping Everest out of the title, thumbnail and opening.
- **What goes with winning:** collage grids, but only for "Every X" list videos (8% vs 1%). Channel logos and series frames are much rarer on winners (3% vs 20%), which mostly reflects big channels.
- **Distinctiveness gate:** 32% of winners pass it vs 24% of the rest, and the drain clones pass 0%. Passing the gate costs nothing.
- **Postcard:** a postcard thumbnail already exists in the Hawaii space. Extremities' "Kalaupapa" video (204K views on 156K subscribers) uses a full-frame vintage "greetings from KALAUPAPA" postcard with a stamp. The niche study's "0 of 106" was true for its own set only. Our postcard needs to look clearly different: a tilted off-white card sitting on the real 3D mountain, no "Greetings from" script, no retro lettering.

**Proposed rule changes** (section 4 of the report):
- Use 1-3 words at 12-18% of thumbnail height, instead of P5's 20%.
- Drop the black caption box with an accent word.
- Replace the absolute brightness target with three checks: the distinctiveness gate, standing out in the dark-mode feed strip, and mid-tone brightness with one bright accent.
- Use no arrows, rings, boxes or numbers.
- Show a partial state rather than a before/after split: the waterline shot (Omaha Beach, 91x subscribers) or a half-lifted lid (Antarctica, 601x).
- Spell Hawaiʻi with the ʻokina, as PBS's "Kīlauea" thumbnail does.

**15 exemplars:**
1. Hawaii's Forgotten Islands
2. RealLifeLore's Hawaii boats video
3. Park Vibes' Niʻihau video
4. PBS Kīlauea
5. Where They Stood's Iwo Jima (1,267x subscribers, the strongest in the set)
6. Where They Stood's Omaha Beach
7. Unseen Works' Antarctica (its lifted-lid image already has 3 copies)
8. Paper Skylines' Australia
9. The Last Day's Nepal flood
10. The Last Day's Lituya Bay
11. Before Humanity's 8 Holes
12. Tetis' Tethys video
13. Astrum Earth's Mariana Trench
14. Fossil
15. Earthyphus

Each one has a line in the report on why it works on a phone, checked against the 168x94 compact-card strip on the contact sheet.

**Caveats:** the sample comes from search results, so successful videos are over-represented. The results are correlations, not causes, and topic and timing confound them. Text heights are visual estimates (within about 2 points).

I wrote the packaging rulebook to `principles.md`. It has 12 testable rules (PK1-PK12) for a faceless map channel, each with the evidence behind it, a pass/fail test and how it applies to ep02. Three findings change the old P1-P9 rules.

**What the evidence changes**
- **Brightness is not what makes a thumbnail win.** In our space the top performers are darker than the rest (median brightness 90 vs 105 on a 0-255 scale). Only 13% of them meet the old rule P5's "40% bright" target, and dark edges are not penalised. P5's "40% bright, never navy" is retired. The new test is relative: our card must be the most distinct one in two dark-mode feed strips, one of clone-lane and Hawaiʻi-lane videos and one of the biggest Hawaiʻi videos.
- **The generic postcard view lost every time it was tested.** In the vidIQ cases, Bolivia's lake panorama lost to one strange close subject (×3.5 views per hour), and the Netherlands' tulips lost to the sea standing above the land (×2.1). "Below the Postcard" works only if the card stays a small object and the real 3D shape dominates the frame.
- **What replaces the face is one "anchor"** next to the main shape. The menu is: a familiar object (the postcard), a true-scale human-sized object, a human trace, a creature from the film, or light and weather. No faces of any kind: faces appear on 5% of winning thumbnails and 12% of the rest.
- **The black caption box is retired** (6% of craft winners use one, 23% of the rest). Graphic devices go to zero. Text is 0-3 words at 12-18% of the frame height, with "HAWAIʻI" spelled with the ʻokina on the card.
- **One new change to the series spec:** no channel logo or wordmark on the thumbnail. Logos and series frames appear on 3% of winners vs 20% of the rest, and Paddy Galloway advises against them. The stamp on the postcard should be a small picture, not the words "Myth Juice".
- **YouTube's Test & Compare picks winners by watch time, not CTR.** The three arms must differ in idea (composition, anchor or state); YouTube says arms that are too similar make tests run longer. YouTube's dynamic thumbnails, announced Sept 2026, make the "three viewers, three arms" design matter more.
- **There is no reliable public CTR benchmark for Suggested vs Browse.** Third-party figures range from 0.6% to 9.5%. Targets stay relative to ep01, measured in the Suggested source only: Suggested CTR of 5% or more, and 15 s or more of watch time per impression (ep01: 5.2 s).
- **New gate bar:** "farther than the craft median" means a distance of at least 11.71 from the drain clones and 11.43 from the template farms. Ep01's own thumbnail clears both and still got 1.97% Suggested CTR, so passing the gate is necessary but not enough.

**The vidIQ call** worked (5 credits) and returned 10 cases: 3 title changes, 6 thumbnail changes and 1 of both. I matched the before/after images to each video and explained each change in section 1.5. The common thread: 5 of 7 thumbnail changes swapped a pretty, generic view for one specific, stranger subject. 6 of 7 new images were less colourful, and 4 of 7 added a human-scale cue without a face (a lantern figure, a boat, an abandoned jacket, a market crowd). The closest title analogue to ep02 is the tsunami video, renamed "The Day 746 Miles Of Earth Suddenly Snapped". It turned a known news label into a physical claim and gained ×2.3.

These cases are weak evidence on their own. Most lifts were from 1-4 views per hour, vidIQ only returns wins, and two of the "winners" were changed again later. I treated them as hypotheses that agree with the larger data sets.

**Ep02:** "Hawaii Is Only the Summit. We Measured the Rest." stays the launch title, as long as the film shows the measurement on screen. The swap for a stall is "Hawaii Is Only the Summit. You Can't See the Rest." "…the Tip…" and "How Tall Is Hawaii, Really?" are rejected. The three thumbnail arms are:
- **A:** the postcard on the drained massif.
- **B:** half-drained, with the card floating on the waterline.
- **C:** the card with no lettering, which tests whether repeating the place name helps.

Paddy Galloway, YouTube's own help pages, MrBeast's production notes and his thumbnail lead are well sourced. Film Booth, Jenny Hoyos and Aprilynne Alter rest on third-party transcripts or summaries, so I weighted them lower. YouTube transcript fetching was blocked as bot-check circumvention, so I did not bypass it. Three recent Creator Insider episodes on thumbnails and A/B tests are worth a human watch; their IDs are in section 7.

The feed simulator is built, both 12-video competitor sets are saved, and the ep01 test does show why ep01 got about 2% CTR. On the small Suggested cards, where 93% of its impressions were, ep01 is the dimmest and hardest-to-read card among bright map thumbnails. It holds up only as a full-width phone card.

**What the simulator does** (`feedsim.py`, built on `work/feedstrip.py`)
- **Three dark-mode layouts at true pixel scale:** the phone Home feed, the phone "Up next" list under a playing video, and the desktop watch-page sidebar. Each gives one screen scrolled so the candidate is visible, plus the full scroll.
- **Text:** Roboto from Google Fonts, titles cut with "…" as YouTube does, and the duration badge. Roboto lacks the ʻokina in "Hawaiʻi", so that one character is drawn in a near-identical fallback font.
- **Options:** a blurred "glance" version per screen, a contact sheet, metrics with the candidate's rank (`--report`), and `--gate` to run the existing distinctiveness gate.
- **Checked:** two runs with the same spec and seed gave identical files.

**Competitor sets** (all in `hosts.json`, thumbnails and avatars beside it, never committed)
- `hawaii` (12): the big Hawaii videos (RealLifeLore, Signore Galilei, Be Smart, Physics Girl, Atlas Pro, Park Vibes, the Hōlei Sea Arch clip, the "Hawaii Is Hiding Something" video) plus drain videos (Unseen Works ×2, Nat Geo Drain the Oceans, Contour Atlas).
- `hawaii_direct` (5): the same-premise drain uploads, which can be mixed in.
- `ep01` (12): continents, Pangaea, map and plate-tectonics videos.
- Views and ages come from YouTube search results, because the sandbox gets blocked on watch pages. Our channel avatar was fetched too.

**Ep01 test** (seed 1, Atlas Pro's Pangaea video playing)
- **Darkest card everywhere:** mean brightness 61 against competitor medians of 98–136. It ranks last on Home (6/6), the sidebar (5/5) and the Up next list (10/10), and last on its brightest areas too. It is a navy field among white relief maps, turquoise seas and bright globes, so it sinks into the dark page.
- **Fails the gate:** 68% blue and 9% red, against limits of 45% and 3%.
- **"Distinct" for the wrong reason:** its distinctiveness score is high (rank 1–2), but that comes from being darker than its neighbours, not from standing out. The README warns about this metric.
- **Small cards (168x94):** "POINTING AT WHAT?" shrinks to letters about 10 px tall, and the arrows, ring and "?" blur into a white squiggle. What is left is orange continents on a map, the same kind of picture as the four Pangaea and supercontinent maps beside it. In the glance version our text is gone, while words like NEW OCEAN and NOT THAT BIG! still read.
- **Title:** the second line goes to the hedge "(Not Just a Coincidence)", and it runs to 3 lines in Up next. The neighbours name concrete things (Bridge, Europe, Africa, Greenland).
- **Full-width phone card:** this one reads fine, which fits Browse/Home's 8.8% CTR. That was only 34 impressions, so it is directional at best.
- **Social proof:** "43 views · 1d ago" next to millions is a gap packaging cannot close.

The simulator cannot predict a CTR number; it shows why ep01 lost next to these particular neighbours. One caveat: many current phone builds show Up next as full-width cards, so the Home layout also stands in for phone Suggested.

I rendered 19 Hawaii hero stills, each at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 (38 files, no text), and documented them in `renders/index.md`. All 19 pass the distinctiveness gate. The one thing not made is the optional tiny tourist (5).

**What was built**
- **Data:** NOAA ETOPO 2022 15" (bathymetry plus land), with AWS Terrain Tiles z11 for land detail on Hawaii and z12 for Everest. ETOPO's sea-floor detail is much sharper than Terrarium's offshore, so it is used under water.
- **Colour:** a cloud-free composite of 48 NASA MODIS days (no August 2023, the Maui fires). Windward cloud is filled from nearby land colour, which leaves smooth green patches visible only in close views.
- **Page:** `engine/www/lab_hawaii.html` has a `SHOTS` table at the top; any field can be overridden with `--q`. Each still renders in 8-15 s. The drain lab and other lab pages were not changed.
- **Seabed look:** dark basalt flanks and dark sediment. Sun shadows are computed live, so any sun angle and exaggeration work.
- **Comparison:** Mauna Loa and Everest are two 28 km blocks on one base line at the same scale. Mauna Loa's column is 17,170 m from summit to true base; Everest is scaled to its surveyed 8,849 m. Ratio as drawn: 1.94.

**Checks**
- **Gate:** 19/19 pass; tan 0-1% (5-9% on Maui Nui from real dry land colour). The first fully drained renders under golden light came out brown and failed (too close to the clones). The final drained shots use neutral daylight on a dark grey basalt floor and pass.
- **Brightness:** mean luma 105-143, no near-black areas.
- **Frame fill:** terrain fills 50-58% in the plates and drained shots, and island plus water fill 59-64% in the half-drained shots.
- **Maui Nui at -400 ft (-122 m):** in the data, Maui and Lana'i join at -59 m and Moloka'i at -79 m. Kaho'olawe only joins at -159 m, so it stays separate, as the brief requires.

**What you should know before picking**
- **True scale is weak from low angles.** A shield volcano at 1.0x reads as a thin band from a low camera, so the low obliques only work at 2x. Those three files are named `_x2` and are for the film only, with "heights exaggerated" said once; the niche report requires 1.0x in the thumbnail. Everything else is 1.0x.
- **Film-only comparison.** The Everest images are banned in thumbnails and in the first 30 s by the niche report and the brief.
- **Drawing aids, not data:** the cream old-shoreline line, the pale band just below it, the foam rim and the gully texture on steep slopes. The shapes themselves are all real data.
- **No tourist (5).** At our 100-450 m grid, a person on the drained cliff is smaller than a pixel. Showing one would need a misleading scale trick. It could be done honestly as a separate paper cut-out shot, clearly not to scale.
- **Repo:** the autosave had already pushed the 24 MB of baked data. I untracked it (it stays on disk and in git history) and git-ignored it except `meta.json`, matching the "data is not committed" rule. The renders and `index.md` will be picked up by the next autosave.

**Best picks**
- **Postcard plate:** `plate_ne` or `plate_ne_wide`, plus `plate_ne_line` with the cyan line on the former coastline.
- **Half drained (-2,400 m):** `half_oblique_w`, `half_east_puna`, `half_contrast_ne`.
- **Mid-drain foam rim (-2,000 m):** `mid_drain_foam_se`.
- **Maui Nui:** `mauinui_400ft_s`.
- **Fully drained:** `drained_massif_e`.

Total disk use is about 170 MB.

pairs.title: Where Does Hawaii Begin? (Not at Sea Level)
pairs.rationale: THE MOMENT, WITH THREE WORDS. Low telephoto from about 40 km off the Hāmākua/Hilo coast at dawn. Mauna Kea's green-and-rust dome (the postcard island) sits on top. Below it a towering dark basalt flank, lit by low warm side light, drops to a white foam rim. Turquoise water fills the bottom. The words IT KEEPS GOING (white, Barlow Condensed 800, soft shadow, no box) sit on the flank just above the waterline, so the text itself points at what the water still hides. TITLE: a twist bracket that cancels the obvious answer (1.56x same-channel; brackets in general 1.30x) on a Where question (1.07x). It is 43 characters (the 41-50 bin), with 'Hawaii' as word 3. The probe found 0 exact matches, and its neighbours are Hawaii-geology videos (SciAm 'How Did Hawaii Form?' 646K, HISTORY 'How the Earth Was Made: Hawaii' 362K, 'The True Size of Hawaii' Short 2.3M), not travel or flood videos. Title and thumbnail share no content words: the title asks, the picture shows that the mountain does not stop at the water. NUMBERS: 3 words on 1 line; cap height 97 px = 13.5% (PK8 range 12-18%); 0 devices; mean luma 120 (target band 95-120); island + flank + water 65% of the frame, sky 35%; warm dawn sky against the hosts' teal and navy. GATE PASS: tan 3%, red 0%, blue 17%. Distance to drain clones 11.93 (bar 11.71) and to template farms 11.64 (bar 11.43). JPEG 134 KB at 1280x720. FEEDSIM: tested among the hawaii hosts in all 3 layouts plus glance. Seeds 2, 5 and 9, plus seed 3 with the same-premise drain uploads mixed in. Luma rank 2-3 of 6 on Home, 3-4 of 10 in Up next, 2-3 of 5 in the sidebar. At 168x94 the words are about 13 px tall and readable, and they still read as a white bar in the blurred glance. ITERATIONS: v1 (Kona coast, cool light) read as a 'dark hill by a lake'. v2 moved to Mauna Kea at -2,400 m with low gold light, but the compact card put the water strip under the duration badge. v3 added more water and moved the text left, away from the badge, but that dropped the farm distance to 11.39. Sky grade and water saturation fixed it. v4 raised the cap height to 13.5%. Clearest single read of the four; my first or second pick for the default arm.
pairs.truth_check: PLATE: our own render (engine/www/lab_hawaii.html) of real NOAA ETOPO 2022 heights with NASA MODIS land colour, at true vertical scale (no exaggeration). The sea is lowered to -2,400 m as a thought experiment, which the film narrates as one ('if we drained it'); the renders index calls this roughly halfway down the submarine flank. The towering look is honest telephoto perspective from a real camera position (154.72W 20.12N, 0.6 km above the lowered water). Nothing is stretched. The foam rim lift, the dawn sky grade and the water saturation are look and grade choices that claim nothing. TEXT: 'IT KEEPS GOING' is true. Below the -2,400 m waterline the flank continues to the sea floor (about -5,000 m or more around the island). For Mauna Loa it continues to its true base about 13 km below sea level (USGS). The brief's cold open says 'The mountain keeps going.' by about 0:04. TITLE: true read as the mountain. Its true base lies far below sea level, and the film pays this off at about 11:20 with 'about 56,000 feet, from its true base' (always naming Mauna Loa). Pedant note: as a land area Hawaii begins at the shoreline; the narration must make clear the film means the mountain. Free of every clone word (drain, hidden, bottom, beneath, nobody, never, found, revealed, sleep, documentary). No Everest, no 'taller', no digits, no source, no AI mention, no emoji, no dropped qualifier.

pairs.title: Hawaii Is Only the Summit. You Can't See the Rest.
pairs.rationale: MAP-NATIVE ANCHOR. Same dawn mid-drain plate as cand_1. A red map pin with a white keyline stands exactly on the old beach, where the green island meets the dark flank. A tiny paper tourist (sun hat, red aloha shirt, white cut-out border) stands at the pin's tip. YOU ARE HERE is set as a map label: dark navy with a white halo, in the sky, no box. Faceless channels can use a familiar interface as the face (Alter on recognisable interfaces; the Google-Maps-card frame at 107x in thumbnail_anatomy). The joke is instant: you are on the beach, and the sea is now far below you. TITLE: the stall-swap B from title_anatomy, a statement plus an access twist ('can't see' 1.56-1.61x same-channel, statement + twist 1.32x). 50 characters, 'Hawaii' first, 0 probe matches. Title says you can't see the rest; the thumbnail shows the rest from where you stand. The only shared word is 'you' (a pronoun, not a content word).
